title: Why a hose nozzle makes water shoot farther
examples: Why does water squirt farther when I cover the end of a hose?
How does a hose nozzle work?
Does a nozzle make more water come out?

explain.say: A hose carries water at a fairly steady rate, a certain number of litres every second, set mostly by the tap and the mains pressure.

draw.text: Why a hose nozzle makes water shoot farther

explain.say: All that water has to get out through the opening at the end. If the opening is made smaller, the same amount of water can only get through by moving faster.
That is why a thumb over the end or a narrow nozzle makes the jet shoot much farther: halve the area of the opening and the water comes out roughly twice as fast.
Making the opening too small does start to cut the flow, because the pressure can only push so much water through, so a nozzle trades flow for speed rather than making more water.

faq.q: Why does water squirt farther when I cover the end of a hose?
faq.a: Covering part of the end makes the opening smaller. The same water has to squeeze through a smaller hole, so it speeds up and flies farther.
asks: How does putting your thumb on a hose work?

faq.q: How does a hose nozzle work?
faq.a: A nozzle narrows the opening, which speeds the water up into a jet. Many nozzles also twist the water or break it up to make a mist or a shower.
asks: What does a spray gun on a hose do?

faq.q: Does a nozzle make more water come out?
faq.a: No. It makes the water come out faster, not in greater amounts. If anything, a very narrow nozzle lets slightly less water through.
asks: Does a nozzle increase water pressure?

faq.q: Why does a faster jet go farther?
faq.a: Water leaving faster travels a longer distance before gravity pulls it to the ground, just like a ball thrown harder.
asks: How far can a hose spray?

faq.q: Why is it called the continuity rule?
faq.a: Engineers call it continuity because water is not created or lost in the pipe: the amount going in each second must equal the amount coming out, so a narrower opening means faster flow.

facts: For a steady flow, the speed of water times the area of the opening stays about the same, so a smaller opening gives a faster jet.
A nozzle increases the speed of the water, not the amount delivered.

quiz.say: You halve the area of a hose opening while the same amount of water flows each second. What happens to its speed?
quiz.show: You halve the area of a hose opening while the same amount of water flows each second. What happens to its speed?
quiz.why: The same volume each second through half the area must move about twice as fast.

wrong.1: A smaller opening speeds the water up, not down.
wrong.2: The water has to speed up to get the same amount through a smaller hole.
